title: Entanglement in bipartite systems with symmetry: coupled chaotic kicked Bose-Hubbard systems
authors: J. Himmelsbach, M. F. I. Kieler, A. Bäcker
abstract: We investigate the average eigenstate entanglement in a bipartite many-body system which exhibits a breaking of two local conservation laws into a global conserved quantity. Such a setting is realized by the particle number conservation in Bose-Hubbard systems. We devise a corresponding random matrix model which captures the universal features of this symmetry breaking and allows for applying powerful random matrix methods. By combining the concept of symmetry resolved entanglement with perturbation theory for quantum chaotic systems we obtain a universal entanglement transition depending on a single fundamental parameter. Furthermore, the symmetry resolved entanglement allows for separating the genuine entanglement from the part which originates from the conserved quantity. This latter contribution is quantified by the number entropy. For this it is shown that the symmetry breaking generates a localization of the eigenstates due to a banded structure of the time-evolution operator. By extrapolating the results beyond the perturbative regime we obtain an analytic description of the full transition.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to measure entanglement in quantum systems where multiple local conservation laws collapse into one global symmetry. By constructing a specialized random matrix model, the authors predict a universal entanglement transition governed by a single parameter. This method successfully separates genuine quantum correlations from those artifacts arising purely from conserved quantities, using Bose-Hubbard models as a key physical example.
main_problem: The study investigates average eigenstate entanglement in bipartite many-body systems where local conservation laws are reduced to a single global conserved quantity.
main_result: A universal entanglement transition is predicted, depending on a single fundamental parameter, which can be separated into genuine quantum correlations and contributions from the conserved quantity via number entropy.
method: The authors employ random matrix theory (RMT) applied to a derived Random Matrix Model (CQTE) that captures the universal features of symmetry breaking in chaotic systems.
model_or_system: The analysis uses coupled kicked Bose-Hubbard systems as an explicit physical realization, modeling the dynamics via time-evolution operators $U$ that exhibit specific symmetries and conservation laws.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy (standard and symmetry resolved), Number entropy, Block entropies ($S_{q_A}$).
important_parameters: The single fundamental parameter governing the entanglement transition ($\Lambda$), coupling strength ($\epsilon$), and system size/dimensionality.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are approximated by quantum chaotic behavior suitable for RMT; specific approximations are made regarding basis state overlaps and sector couplings in the perturbative analysis.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the bipartite system with a conserved quantity. Figure 2 shows realizations of the CQTE across varying coupling strengths ($\epsilon$). Figure 3 compares density operators $ho_A$ at different coupling strengths. Figure 11 plots average linear entanglement entropy $S_2$ vs $\sqrt{\Lambda N}$ for the kicked Bose-Hubbard model.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general framework using symmetry-resolved entanglement, develops a corresponding random matrix ensemble (CQTE), and then applies this formalism to analyze the transition from uncoupled to strongly interacting regimes in the specific example of coupled kicked Bose-Hubbard systems.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful theoretical tools—symmetry-resolved measures and RMT techniques—to quantify entanglement in complex, interacting quantum many-body systems exhibiting underlying symmetries or conservation laws, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and quantum chaos in condensed matter models.
